# Streaming Breusch-Pagan test for large datasets

<small>Source: [`R/performance.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/performance.R) · Help: `?performBPTestStreaming`</small>

Computes the classical Breusch-Pagan statistic chunk by chunk so that large
datasets can be evaluated without materialising the full auxiliary regression in
memory. The streamed result is algebraically identical to
[`performBPTest`](performBPTest.md).

## Usage

```r
performBPTestStreaming(model, data = NULL, chunk_size = 10000, progress = interactive())
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted [stats::lm](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) object describing the mean structure whose
    residual variance is to be assessed.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, or `NULL`, the default, read as [`performWhiteTestStreaming()`](performWhiteTestStreaming.md) reads it: the response, design, weights and offset come from the fit itself, so a model that transforms its variables, has an `offset()` term, or takes its `weights` or `offset` from a column of the data needs no `data` (since 0.16.0), and data that are given are matched to the observations of the fit.

`chunk_size`
:   Positive integer giving the number of observations processed per
    streaming chunk. Smaller values reduce peak memory usage at the expense of
    additional iteration overhead.

`progress`
:   Logical flag controlling whether a textual progress bar is displayed
    while chunks are processed. Defaults to `interactive()`.

## Value

A `htest` object mirroring [`performBPTest`](performBPTest.md) and reporting the
chi-squared statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, and metadata describing the
chunked computation.

## Details

Each chunk of the regressors, centred at their means, is reduced by a QR
decomposition stacked on the triangular factor of the chunks before it, as in
[`performWhiteTestStreaming()`](performWhiteTestStreaming.md), since 0.17.0. Up to 0.16.0 the
cross-products of the regressors were accumulated: those of a regressor 1,000
standard deviations from zero looked collinear with the intercept, and the test
stopped ("Breusch-Pagan auxiliary regression became rank deficient"); and squared
residuals of about \(10^{-10}\) were taken for constant ("requires variation in
squared residuals"). It gives the value of [`performBPTest()`](performBPTest.md) on both.
Sparse cross-products from Matrix are no longer used.

Since 0.16.0 the chunks are rows of the design of the fit, as in
[`performWhiteTestStreaming()`](performWhiteTestStreaming.md), whose details say what changed.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit, and, since 0.16.0, a multivariate `lm`, a fit changed after it
was fitted and a fit with `model = FALSE` whose data are gone, unless `data` gives its
response and fitted values. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## See also

[`performBPTest`](performBPTest.md) for the standard implementation.

## Examples

```r
data(mtcars)
mod <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
performBPTestStreaming(mod, mtcars, chunk_size = 16, progress = FALSE)
```
